Q: Logical address space in 64-bit and 32-bit OS A:

Sort of, but there are many technicalities which make these names less useful.

First, there are two different sizes that matter to an operating system: Address size and data size. The address size determines how big of an address space is available, and the data size determines how much data can be used in a single-word operation. In my experience, operating systems are usually identified by data size, which means the address size could be something else.

Below are some example architectures and their address and data sizes. As the table shows, the most common 32 bit and 64 bit architectures today have the same data and address sizes, which is why your statement is partially correct. Note that x86 processors in 16-bit mode have a larger address size than data size. This is caused by additional segment registers being used in addressing, which makes the architecture less restrictive.

                 Address size      Data size
x86 16-bit        20 bits           16 bits
x86 32-bit        32 bits           32 bits
x86 64-bit        64 bits           64 bits
ARM 32-bit        32 bits           32 bits
ARM 64-bit        64 bits           64 bits

However, the address size does not necessarily indicate how big of a logical address space can be used. There could be a limitation which restricts the space to a smaller area. For example, no current x86-64 processor supports a 64 bit address space. Instead, they require that the high 16 bits of any address be a sign extension of bit 47, allowing a 248 address space, 256 TiB instead of 16 EiB. This reduces the number of address lines which need to be used in the processor while allowing far more than anyone currently uses.

Finally, everything so far has been in reference to the logical or virtual address space. The physical address space could have a different size. Newer 32 bit x86 systems have Physical Address Extension, which enables 36 bit physical addresses, and x86-64 systems are limited to no more than a 52 bit physical address space, but this can be further limited by the memory controller/motherboard. When the logical address space is bigger than the physical address space, it allows the entire physical address space to be mapped to multiple places at once. When the logical address space is smaller, it allows multiple complete address spaces to be stored in physical memory at the same time.

Q: How can I print the value of a Tensor object in TensorFlow? A:

It has worked with TensorFlow version 2.4.1:

import tensorflow as tf
tf.config.run_functions_eagerly(True)  # Forces eager execution
# (...) your tensor named 'my_tensor' is created
print(my_tesor.numpy())

Watch out for methods annotated with the @tf.function:

Long story short:

If @tf.function is not necessary, try removing it. When @tf.function is applied, the code is compiled to run in graph mode, which does not support .numpy() directly. Instead, remove it so that the function can run in eager mode by default - by ChatGPT :-).

Finally, guys, consider checking the newer TensorFlow versions which, to my understanding, offer better debugging and value reading (internal state) alternatives.

Q: How to reduce PDF file size for while generating PDF from chrome print option A:

There are several types of compression used inside a PDF especially for images and thus some users confused by an increase when some are altered.

THe OP had issues where some jpgs we re-encoded as larger encodings.

Usually, an optimised one will have been used by the Author or Producer and in some cases, there may be no significant change in file size.

The encoded parts use /Named"Filters" such as ASCIIHexDecode, ASCII85Decode, LZWDecode, FlateDecode, RunLengthDecode, CCITTFaxDecode, JBIG2Decode, DCTDecode, JPXDecode, and new kid BrotliDecode (not yet supported by many PDF Readers)!

So, what is a good strategy when attempting reduction is to try to use JPXDecode (Lossless or lossy) for images and basic high speed /FlateDecode for as much of the other objects. Also DO NOT /Linearize if possible.

The differences are

  • /Linearize MUST add extra server overheads and not be of any value to recipients (only "Web Enhanced" servers).

  • /FlateDecode (also known as Deflate) is the fastest ZIPped compression for PDF Readers. PNG is not native to PDF and thus PNGs will often become 2 parts of /FlateDecode such as lossless bitmap and their /Softmask overlay[s]. Any other exotic compression is more time consuming for everyone.

  • /DCTDecode is the native lossy compression for JPEG standard RGB images and is one native format allowed in a PDF image. This is not the best if Q(uality) is reduced.

  • /JPXDecode introduced in PDF-1.5 (August 2003) is most recently the best compressive and thus extra time for compress and decompress handling, so often not used as much as it could be. However, it is the current "almost" fully compressed of PDF lossless/lossy filters.

  • Some compression/decompression filters may be combined with others even one of each to reduce increased file size.

There are current recent experimental PDF ones such as /BrotliDecode (10 years old!) and the issue here is it adds extra development time and is unlikely to work in many readers even current Acrobats, so non compatible with the bulk of PDF users.

Heavily used by web developers but not often found in PDF.

Brotli is an open source general-purpose data compressor introduced by Google in late 2013 and now adopted in most known browsers and Web servers. It is publicly available on GitHub and its data format was submitted as RFC 7932 in July 2016.

Only this year 2025 has it been suggested as adopted for PDF widespread "catch up". Some readers have started to use it as part of adoption of PDF 2.0

Oddly, although heavily used by Google, Chrome currently does not support it!

Answer

Since neither of the 2 most compressive formats will currently suit the OP question. We are left with the more common WEB PNG or JPEG formats and thus for the "photo" images only the smaller JPEG format is going to make some difference thus ALL the PNGs need conversion to lesser JPG (DCT) images. Since the WEB canvas notional density is 96 dpi then for the same quality as the web screen use 96dpi JPGs and keep the Q value around 95 if replacing PNGs for photos you can try Q80.

Then the filesize as PDF will be much smaller.

Q: AttributeError on 'mediapipe' module A:

You are encountering this error because in MediaPipe 0.10.x, the Python API has changed and the solutions namespace is no longer exposed at the top-level mediapipe module.

In older versions, this worked:

import mediapipe as mp
mp.solutions.

But in MediaPipe ≥ 0.10, solutions is not available directly under mediapipe, which causes:

AttributeError: module 'mediapipe' has no attribute 'solutions'

✅ Correct approach

Import the Hands solution eexplicitly:

from mediapipe.python.solutions import hands
self.mp_hands = hands

Or directly instantiate it:

from mediapipe.python.solutions.hands import Hands

self.mp_hands = Hands()

🔎 Why this happens

According to the MediaPipe Python package structure introduced in 0.10.x, solution modules are located under:

mediapipe.python.solutions

and are not re-exported at the package root.

🔁 Alternative workaround

If you want to keep legacy code unchanged, downgrade MediaPipe:

pip install mediapipe==0.9.3

📌 Summary

This is not a bug, but an API change

mp.solutions no longer exists in MediaPipe 0.10.x

Import solutions directly from mediapipe.python.solutions

Q: How to get Details on Discount from a Subscription in Stripe? A:

https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/object states to:

Use expand[]=discounts to expand each discount.

To do this using the ruby gem, run the following:

Stripe::Subscription.retrieve(id: "sub_....", expand: ['discounts'])

Q: Modern C++ way to copy string into char* A:

If you're using a POSIX-compatible system, use strdup.

#include <string.h>

char *strdup(const char *s);

The strdup() function returns a pointer to a new string which is a duplicate of the string s. Memory for the new string is obtained with malloc(3), and can be freed with free(3).
